title: Gather — A collection of portfolio resources

links.description: A roundup of niche, tightly curated inspiration sites full of real tech-industry work — a better starting point than endless Pinterest scrolling.
Malik's site for Yale architecture student Anaelle Blin. The hero is a mind map of connected images, so you see the thinking behind the work, not just the finished projects.
&Walsh's Bombas refresh. A clear example of presenting a brand system: soft shapes, rounded type, palette and art direction shown working across every sub-brand.
Recruitment site for Quebec's independent live-music scene. Warped, poster-like type and a hot pink and black palette bring the energy of the stage to the screen.
A space for music makers to share their sound. Instead of a standard hero, drifting blurred shapes and a pixelated orb set the mood before any content appears.
Swiss designer Cedric Hofstetter's one-page portfolio. A clean, neo-brutalist build set entirely in a mono typeface, with a technical, table-style layout and sections that open and close.
Photo-real mockups for presenting your work: devices, print, packaging, apparel and billboards, plus a free mockup library. Most are paid, and often on sale.
Jean Create's identity for PORO, shown on Akoya mockups. Bold type, playful shapes and unexpected color pairings. Every piece looks different but still belongs to one visual world.
Studio site for Monstro, an LA creative practice. Oversized type that runs off the edges and turns on its side makes the homepage feel like a poster you scroll through.
Savee zooms through eight saved favorites, from Balenciaga down to an empty mountain road. A playful way to present a collection, and a reminder that motion can carry a portfolio.
A round-up of work designers have saved on Savee, the visual bookmarking site. Worth setting up an account to build your own reference library.
Los Caballos' social system for Brooklyn venue Public Records. Expressive templates for each kind of night, plus a plain, legible line-up template that handles three rooms at once.
Templates and mockups for presenting work: portfolio layouts, mood and art direction boards, and in-studio photo mockups. Works in Canva, Figma, Google Slides and InDesign.
Situation Normal's launch post for its new studio site, built around “the work that built the studio.” A good model for announcing your own portfolio.
A designer's favorite finds from one month: sites that sparked new ideas, collected into one carousel. Good starting points for building your own resource list.
Studio Miles' full identity redesign for Café Saint-Henri, a Quebec specialty coffee roaster. Shows how to preview a visual system that balances tradition and modernity.
Analogue's Sprite × NBA platform: 17 city cans, a “fractured court” design system, retail and merch. A case study that lets the visuals do most of the talking, with short, sharp text.
A handmade Instax Mini double case, with a free template in the creator's bio. A tactile idea for a leave-behind or self-promo piece.
Netzzy's “The Everything Store,” a generative archival study built from Amazon product data in TouchDesigner. A reference for personal projects that push into data and code.
Juliette's portfolio (gougoucore.com), built in Readymag. A big serif statement up top, then numbered projects with tactile, hands-on photography.
AIGA NY Fall Portfolio Review — Fri, Nov 13, 2–6pm at Parsons (65 W 11th St). Two 15-minute one-on-one reviews; $20 members, $30 non-members. Spots fill fast.
A curated list of portfolios that feel like they moved from the physical world into the digital: personal, tactile and full of small details. Comment “INSPO” on the post for the link.
Company Policy is hiring conceptual, tech-forward designers of all levels. Remote (ET hours), full-time. Send your portfolio to careers@companypolicy.studio by Oct 24, 2026.
A daily-updated showcase of well-designed websites, browsable by style, type and subject, including a Portfolio category.
Vianna Kwok's “233 Days in Loeb Hall,” a 183-page, one-color scarlet riso book. A reminder that a portfolio piece can be a printed object.
